analysis:
All three changed files are test-only Swift files: DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift (lines 77, 86-87, 138-139), StatusCommandRunTests.swift (lines 82-84, 100-141), and the new DaemonStateServedCountTests.swift. The changes update expected operator-facing wording. Served-request counts are now scoped to the daemon session and counted as output tokens. A cancellations_partial_complete count is shown as requests that ended early and may be unpaid. One new test checks that the daemon state file carries that count.

No production code is in the supplied diff, so no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, the coordinator-provider WebSocket, prefix-cache storage or the fan helper can be assessed from it. The tests use temporary sandboxes (CLICommandSandbox, a temporary directory) and a stub coordinator (CoordinatorStub), with no real credentials. The new test writes only to a UUID-named temporary directory and removes it afterwards. The state fields involved are non-secret counters, so no data-exposure regression is visible. The test constructs ProviderLoop with attestationSigner nil and an unreachable coordinator URL (ws://127.0.0.1:0), and nothing connects to a real coordinator.

Remaining integration question, outside the supplied evidence: the production code that writes cancellations_partial_complete into daemon-state.json and renders the new status and doctor messages. Reviewers should confirm it adds only counters and does not weaken any trust or billing control. The tests are not evidence of those production changes. The "may be unpaid" statement is operator guidance, not a security control. No threat-model update is required from these test-only changes.
